key_insight: Dynin-Robotics unifies vision, language, goal prediction, and action generation in a single diffusion-based trajectory model for robot control. Instead of using separate modules, the same omnimodal backbone can condition on different inputs and predict either desired outcomes or action-dependent scene changes.
problem_solved: Robotic policies often struggle to connect language instructions, visual context, future goals, and executable actions in one coherent framework. This paper addresses the challenge of generating and selecting actions while also predicting where the scene should end up and how it changes over time.
method: Builds on Dynin-Omni, an omnimodal masked-diffusion backbone that represents language, visual observations, goals, and actions as discrete tokens.
Uses a shared trajectory model to support both visual goal prediction and dynamics prediction as conditioning signals for action generation and selection.
Varies conditioning and target spans within the same model to flexibly handle different robot control and prediction tasks.
impact: This matters because it points toward more unified robot policies that can reason about both what to do and what the world should look like afterward. For AI/ML practitioners, it suggests a scalable architecture for multimodal decision-making without relying on many task-specific models.

paper_title: Dynin-Robotics: Omnimodal Unified Diffusion Vision-Language-Action Model
paper_authors: Hoeun Lee, Jaeik Kim, Jusang Oh, Jinhyeok Kim, Geon Choi
